# The doctrine as do's and don'ts

**Generated by `npm run doctrine`. Do not edit — edit `src/data/design-doctrine.json`.**

The reasoning, the trigger and Rahul's verbatim words live in the JSON and are the part worth reading twice. This page is the other half: the same lessons reduced to lines you can check a screen against without re-reading an essay. dd-016 exists because a cited principle is not an instruction.

21 entries · 121 rules · 15 entries bind any calculator screen

---

## Before you design a calculator screen

Every one of these must be answered by id in the component's `.checks.md`.
Generate the skeleton with `npm run doctrine:checks <ComponentName>`.

- `dd-001/dont-1` Don't delete a capability in order to make a screen simpler.
- `dd-001/dont-2` Don't read 'three inputs' as the offering; it is the entry only.
- `dd-002/dont-1` Don't measure layering by the volume of content revealed.
- `dd-002/dont-2` Don't reveal more than about two new controls or concepts in a single step.
- `dd-003/dont-1` Don't let a screen's only takeaway be a number.
- `dd-003/dont-2` Don't mistake capability for achievement.
- `dd-004/dont-1` Don't reconcile two number systems in a footnote, caption or parenthetical.
- `dd-004/dont-2` Don't use the words real and nominal as if the reader already holds them.
- `dd-005/dont-1` Don't hand the reader a list of things to worry about and call it completeness.
- `dd-006/dont-1` Don't swap one body of text for a nearly identical one.
- `dd-006/dont-2` Don't hide half of a difference behind a control when the difference is the lesson.
- `dd-007/dont-1` Don't cascade font sizes because it looks better.
- `dd-007/dont-2` Don't render a hierarchy that does not exist.
- `dd-008/dont-1` Don't rewrite a sentence as a control moves.
- `dd-008/dont-2` Don't describe where the reader currently is.
- `dd-009/dont-1` Don't show a figure that differs from a stated assumption without saying why, in the same breath.
- `dd-009/dont-2` Don't shorten a screen by deleting an explanation.
- `dd-010/dont-1` Don't headline a terminal balance, or any other accountant's summary.
- `dd-012/dont-1` Don't headline an average taken over situations the feature was never meant to affect.
- `dd-012/dont-2` Don't make a difference of two averages the verdict line.
- `dd-012/dont-3` Don't ship a screen that leaves the reader confused, however correct its figures.
- `dd-013/dont-1` Don't give a new surface its own inputs, worker, seed or simulation count.
- `dd-013/dont-2` Don't let one quantity appear twice on a page with two values.
- `dd-017/dont-1` Don't take a multi-year input as a bare number and let it decay in silence.
- `dd-017/dont-2` Don't put a question in the unit the engine finds convenient rather than the one the reader thinks in.
- `dd-017/dont-3` Don't turn the fix into a mode question at the entry; state the interpretation instead of asking for it.
- `dd-017/dont-4` Don't let a step-up of zero mean the reader's real saving falls every year.
- `dd-017/dont-5` Don't state a goal in today's money beside a contribution in tomorrow's without saying they differ.
- `dd-019/dont-1` Don't split a number across a label, a stat block and a caption, as in 'THE SAME MONEY / Rs 9.43 Lakh / in today's prices'.
- `dd-019/dont-2` Don't attach the same frame phrase to more than one quantity on a screen without naming each one.
- `dd-019/dont-3` Don't treat a correct frame as sufficient disambiguation; T8 was applied correctly here and the screen was still ambiguous.
- `dd-019/dont-4` Don't use a heading that reads as a claim of equivalence ('THE SAME MONEY') when it means 'this sum, re-expressed'.
- `dd-020/dont-1` Don't hide an option because it is unlikely - unlikely is not inapplicable, and the reader it fits never learns it was there.
- `dd-020/dont-2` Don't ask a question that does not go on to remove something - a question that buys no simplification is pure cost.
- `dd-020/dont-3` Don't let a category filter change a computed answer; it removes what cannot apply, never what is inconvenient to support.

## Every entry

### dd-000 — Why this file exists

*process — how we keep records*

**Do**

- `dd-000/do-1` Record the spirit in this file BEFORE acting on the feedback.
- `dd-000/do-2` Keep the verbatim words exactly, spelling and punctuation included.
- `dd-000/do-3` Give every entry a test that can be answered on paper.
- `dd-000/do-4` Answer the relevant tests before designing, while the design is still cheap to change.
- `dd-000/do-5` Treat a small trigger as evidence of a principle that may govern everything.

**Don't**

- `dd-000/dont-1` Don't paraphrase, tidy or shorten the verbatim quote.
- `dd-000/dont-2` Don't act first and record afterwards.
- `dd-000/dont-3` Don't answer a twice-broken rule with a firmer intention instead of a mechanism.
- `dd-000/dont-4` Don't treat a recorded lesson as a filed one; an unconsulted doctrine is an archive.

> **Test.** Before any design or UX decision this file is read, and each relevant entry's test is answered explicitly for the thing being designed. Any principle here violated twice is a process failure, not a mistake.

### dd-001 — The offering is all the complexity, packaged - never reduced

*calculators · articles · homepage · illustrations*

**Do**

- `dd-001/do-1` Move complexity to a deeper layer and keep it reachable.
- `dd-001/do-2` Absorb the difficulty of packaging into our work, never the reader's.
- `dd-001/do-3` Within a filtered set, offer every eligible option rather than a curated shortlist.

**Don't**

- `dd-001/dont-1` Don't delete a capability in order to make a screen simpler.
- `dd-001/dont-2` Don't read 'three inputs' as the offering; it is the entry only.

> **Test.** For any simplification, ask: did the complexity move, or did it disappear? If a capability is no longer reachable by a determined user, this has been violated.

### dd-002 — Layer by the user's next question, not by volume of content

*calculators · interactive components · workbenches*

**Do**

- `dd-002/do-1` Open each layer on one question the reader is actually having, in the order they have it.
- `dd-002/do-2` Expose one control and one consequence per step, then hand off to the next question.

**Don't**

- `dd-002/dont-1` Don't measure layering by the volume of content revealed.
- `dd-002/dont-2` Don't reveal more than about two new controls or concepts in a single step.

> **Test.** Count the controls and new concepts revealed by a single disclosure step. More than about two means the step is a cliff. Every step must be answerable: which question of the user's does this answer?

### dd-003 — The user pays in time and attention

*calculators · articles · homepage · the whole product*

**Do**

- `dd-003/do-1` Give every screen one transferable idea the reader could use without us.
- `dd-003/do-2` Treat correct maths and full features as the price of admission.

**Don't**

- `dd-003/dont-1` Don't let a screen's only takeaway be a number.
- `dd-003/dont-2` Don't mistake capability for achievement.

> **Test.** For every screen: what idea does the user leave with that they did not arrive with, and could they now use it without us? If the honest answer is 'a number', that screen has taken payment without delivering.

### dd-004 — Never use a concept the reader has not been given

*calculators · articles · illustrations · any figure projected forward*

**Do**

- `dd-004/do-1` Carry each figure's frame on the figure itself, visibly and permanently.
- `dd-004/do-2` Default to today's money; make future rupees the thing the reader opts into.
- `dd-004/do-3` Teach a distinction on its own step, in the reader's words, before relying on it.

**Don't**

- `dd-004/dont-1` Don't reconcile two number systems in a footnote, caption or parenthetical.
- `dd-004/dont-2` Don't use the words real and nominal as if the reader already holds them.

> **Test.** Point at any number on any screen. Can the reader say which money it is in, without scrolling and without knowing the words real or nominal? If not, this is violated.

### dd-005 — Find the one comparison the whole subject reduces to

*calculators · articles*

**Do**

- `dd-005/do-1` Name the single comparison the whole subject reduces to, and put it on screen.
- `dd-005/do-2` Introduce every other factor as a push on one side of that comparison.

**Don't**

- `dd-005/dont-1` Don't hand the reader a list of things to worry about and call it completeness.

> **Test.** For any calculator, name the single comparison it reduces to. If there isn't one, the model has not been found yet and the screen is still a list.

### dd-006 — Never make the reader diff two states

*calculators · interactive components · any toggle, tab or mode*

**Do**

- `dd-006/do-1` Show both views adjacently when both of them matter.
- `dd-006/do-2` Reserve a toggle for genuine alternatives the reader is choosing between.

**Don't**

- `dd-006/dont-1` Don't swap one body of text for a nearly identical one.
- `dd-006/dont-2` Don't hide half of a difference behind a control when the difference is the lesson.

> **Test.** Flip the control and watch your own eyes. If you have to hunt for what changed, the reader will fail where you merely struggled. Prefer adjacency to alternation.

### dd-007 — Every visual difference must mean something

*calculators · articles · illustrations · every screen*

**Do**

- `dd-007/do-1` State what each difference in size, weight or colour asserts.
- `dd-007/do-2` Make equal things look equal; isolate the one thing that matters more.

**Don't**

- `dd-007/dont-1` Don't cascade font sizes because it looks better.
- `dd-007/dont-2` Don't render a hierarchy that does not exist.

> **Test.** For each difference in size, weight or colour on a screen, state what it asserts. If the answer is 'it looked better', remove it and make the elements equal.

### dd-008 — A control changes what you SEE, never what you have to RE-READ

*calculators · interactive components · any slider, stepper or dial*

**Do**

- `dd-008/do-1` Put live values in fixed slots the eye can return to.
- `dd-008/do-2` Write prose as principles that stay true at every position of every control.
- `dd-008/do-3` State the boundary — where the plan breaks — instead of the current state.
- `dd-008/do-4` Mark that boundary on the control's own track.

**Don't**

- `dd-008/dont-1` Don't rewrite a sentence as a control moves.
- `dd-008/dont-2` Don't describe where the reader currently is.

> **Test.** Drag the control from one end to the other. Does any sentence change? If yes, that sentence was describing a state rather than a principle or a boundary, and it belongs in a fixed slot as a value instead.

### dd-009 — Simplicity is removing WORK, not removing INFORMATION

*calculators · articles · illustrations · every screen*

**Do**

- `dd-009/do-1` Make every number traceable from what is already on the screen.
- `dd-009/do-2` Name a thing, and how often it happens, before using it.
- `dd-009/do-3` Do the arithmetic for the reader; the tool processes, the reader absorbs.

**Don't**

- `dd-009/dont-1` Don't show a figure that differs from a stated assumption without saying why, in the same breath.
- `dd-009/dont-2` Don't shorten a screen by deleting an explanation.

> **Test.** Read the screen as someone who knows nothing. Count the questions it raises that it does not answer. That count is the real cognitive load, and it is not reduced by having fewer words.

### dd-010 — Measure the lived experience, not the accountant's summary

*calculators · articles*

**Do**

- `dd-010/do-1` Headline the quantity a person actually lives through, month to month.
- `dd-010/do-2` Let the summary figure sit beside it as context.

**Don't**

- `dd-010/dont-1` Don't headline a terminal balance, or any other accountant's summary.

> **Test.** Ask what the person would actually feel, month to month, living inside this projection. If the headline figure is not something they would ever experience, it is the wrong headline.

### dd-011 — A record with no failure mode will drift, and an expensive record will be skipped

*process — how we keep records*

**Do**

- `dd-011/do-1` Give every durable store a detector that names what is missing and what to do.
- `dd-011/do-2` Keep the record inside the repository, where the tooling can see it.
- `dd-011/do-3` Reduce the cost of compliance; laboriousness is itself a cause of drift.
- `dd-011/do-4` Say what an artefact will cost to maintain before building it.

**Don't**

- `dd-011/dont-1` Don't answer a broken rule by restating it more firmly.
- `dd-011/dont-2` Don't build a designed document when a list was asked for.

> **Test.** For each store we rely on: what breaks, visibly, if it is neglected for a week? If the answer is 'nothing', it is already drifting and we simply cannot see it yet.

### dd-012 — Judge a thing by the situation it exists for, not by an average over all situations

*calculators · articles · any feature that exists for the tail*

**Do**

- `dd-012/do-1` Show the feature in the situation it exists for — for protection, the bad futures.
- `dd-012/do-2` State as plainly what a protection does not cover as what it does.

**Don't**

- `dd-012/dont-1` Don't headline an average taken over situations the feature was never meant to affect.
- `dd-012/dont-2` Don't make a difference of two averages the verdict line.
- `dd-012/dont-3` Don't ship a screen that leaves the reader confused, however correct its figures.

> **Test.** Name the situation the feature exists for. Is that situation on the screen? If the headline is an average taken over all situations, including the many the feature was never meant to affect, the wrong measure is being reported. And point at the verdict line: can the reader picture a single concrete instance of that quantity? If not, replace it.

### dd-013 — One engine. Two surfaces may never show different numbers for the same input

*calculators · any page with more than one view of the same computation*

**Do**

- `dd-013/do-1` Compute once per set of inputs and distribute that one result to every surface.
- `dd-013/do-2` Build the simple view as a projection of the expert one.
- `dd-013/do-3` Assert in a test that the two surfaces agree on every shared number.

**Don't**

- `dd-013/dont-1` Don't give a new surface its own inputs, worker, seed or simulation count.
- `dd-013/dont-2` Don't let one quantity appear twice on a page with two values.

> **Test.** Change one input and read every figure on the page. Does any quantity appear twice with two values? If two surfaces can be made to disagree by any input, they are two engines and the page is lying to somebody.

### dd-014 — Use native HTML/CSS for bespoke infographics, not SVGs

*articles · illustrations · artifacts · infographics*

**Do**

- `dd-014/do-1` Build infographics natively as Astro components in HTML and Tailwind.
- `dd-014/do-2` Ship the actual visual artifacts before calling a draft finished.

**Don't**

- `dd-014/dont-1` Don't propose or ship an SVG asset for a bespoke infographic.
- `dd-014/dont-2` Don't leave a placeholder such as [SVG_PROPOSAL] in a finished article.

> **Test.** Scan the article for SVGs or placeholders. If the visual explanation relies on an external SVG file or a text placeholder rather than a native HTML/CSS component, this rule has been violated.

### dd-015 — The Template is the Floor, not the Prose (Bespoke Subheadings and Stealth Learning)

*articles · headers*

**Do**

- `dd-015/do-1` Write every header as an editorial proposition that advances the argument.
- `dd-015/do-2` Treat the dossier sections as a conceptual checklist, a floor to clear.
- `dd-015/do-3` Teach the abstraction by stealth, layer by layer, without announcing the lesson.

**Don't**

- `dd-015/dont-1` Don't use internal dossier labels (TL;DR, Hook, Mechanism, Rupee Spine) as MDX headers.
- `dd-015/dont-2` Don't use banned meta-language such as 'First Principles' or 'This guide'.

> **Test.** Skim only the headers. Do they read like an essay outline (PASS) or a bureaucratic form (FAIL)? Search the text for explicitly banned meta-language; if present, it fails.

### dd-016 — A lesson is not followable until it has been reduced to do's and don'ts

*process — how we keep records*

**Do**

- `dd-016/do-1` Extract the do's and don'ts into the entry itself, in the same turn it is recorded.
- `dd-016/do-2` Write each line as one imperative that can be checked without reading the entry it came from.
- `dd-016/do-3` Read the generated docs/doctrine-rules.md before designing anything.
- `dd-016/do-4` Answer the don'ts that apply, by id, in the component's .checks.md.

**Don't**

- `dd-016/dont-1` Don't record an entry without its do's and don'ts - extraction is part of recording, not a follow-up.
- `dd-016/dont-2` Don't hand-edit docs/doctrine-rules.md; it is a projection of the JSON and dd-013 governs it.
- `dd-016/dont-3` Don't cite an entry in a checks file and leave its don'ts unanswered. That is the dd-012 failure exactly.
- `dd-016/dont-4` Don't write a do or a don't that needs its own paragraph to be understood. If it cannot be a line, it is not yet extracted.

> **Test.** Open docs/doctrine-rules.md. Could a reviewer who has never read the doctrine check a screen against it, line by line? Every entry must appear there with at least one do and one don't, and every checks file must answer the don'ts that apply to it by id.

### dd-017 — Ask for an input in the same money you report the answer in

*calculators · any input that persists over more than a year · entry contracts*

**Do**

- `dd-017/do-1` Ask for a lasting input in the same money the answer is reported in.
- `dd-017/do-2` Interpret a monthly contribution as real by default, and say plainly that this is what is being run.
- `dd-017/do-3` Make a step-up an optional REAL increment for career progression, on top of a base that already holds purchasing power.
- `dd-017/do-4` Give the salaried a share-of-income framing and the self-employed an inflation-linked one - same arithmetic, two vocabularies.
- `dd-017/do-5` Show what a real-terms contribution becomes in cash later, so the reader can check they could keep it up.
- `dd-017/do-6` Treat symmetry with the other side of the product as a design test: would the same person, drawing down, be asked this way?

**Don't**

- `dd-017/dont-1` Don't take a multi-year input as a bare number and let it decay in silence.
- `dd-017/dont-2` Don't put a question in the unit the engine finds convenient rather than the one the reader thinks in.
- `dd-017/dont-3` Don't turn the fix into a mode question at the entry; state the interpretation instead of asking for it.
- `dd-017/dont-4` Don't let a step-up of zero mean the reader's real saving falls every year.
- `dd-017/dont-5` Don't state a goal in today's money beside a contribution in tomorrow's without saying they differ.

> **Test.** Read the entry fields and the headline together. Are they in the same money? If the answer is in today's prices and any input is not, name which. And count the questions the entry asks: stating an interpretation is allowed, asking the reader to choose one at step one is not.

### dd-018 — Flowing prose over choppy sentences

*articles · content factory · prose · content_drafter · content_evaluator*

**Do**

- `dd-018/do-1` Write in flowing, cohesive paragraphs that sustain an analytical argument, matching the pacing of 'The Loss That Never Happened'.
- `dd-018/do-2` Anchor an abstract tax rule in one named person's concrete conflict, as Section 50CA is anchored in Arjun Mehta's sale.
- `dd-018/do-3` State the government's own economic motive for a rule - the State's Perspective - not only its mechanics.
- `dd-018/do-4` Use strong, structural analogies (e.g., slicing a pizza, the 5 share prices) to translate technical depth without losing the reader.
- `dd-018/do-5` Study 'The Loss That Never Happened' for mechanical pacing and flow.
- `dd-018/do-6` Study the rewritten 'The Price You Didn't Receive' for narrative anchoring and associative explainability.

**Don't**

- `dd-018/dont-1` Don't write choppy, half-a-line, or single-sentence paragraphs like the original draft of 'The Price You Didn't Receive'.
- `dd-018/dont-2` Don't confuse simplicity of explanation with primitive, staccato sentence structures.
- `dd-018/dont-3` Don't atomise a deep, complex argument into disjointed fragments that destroy the pacing and reading experience.
- `dd-018/dont-4` Don't produce 'lazy AI slop' that blindly lists facts without weaving them into a cohesive, magazine-style narrative.

> **Test.** Read the draft aloud. Does it flow like a cohesive, authoritative article in a premium magazine, or does it sound like a disjointed slide presentation? Are the paragraphs properly structured with complete sentences?

### dd-019 — A number is a quantity, an amount and a frame

*calculators · answer layers · rungs · articles · any surface printing a figure*

**Do**

- `dd-019/do-1` Write quantity + amount + frame as one phrase on one line, in that order: 'Rs 9.14 lakh more, in today's prices'.
- `dd-019/do-2` Put the noun that says what a figure counts on the same line as the figure itself.
- `dd-019/do-3` When two figures on one screen share a frame, make the noun the thing that tells them apart.
- `dd-019/do-4` Name the quantity even when the frame alone feels sufficient - the unit is not the quantity.

**Don't**

- `dd-019/dont-1` Don't split a number across a label, a stat block and a caption, as in 'THE SAME MONEY / Rs 9.43 Lakh / in today's prices'.
- `dd-019/dont-2` Don't attach the same frame phrase to more than one quantity on a screen without naming each one.
- `dd-019/dont-3` Don't treat a correct frame as sufficient disambiguation; T8 was applied correctly here and the screen was still ambiguous.
- `dd-019/dont-4` Don't use a heading that reads as a claim of equivalence ('THE SAME MONEY') when it means 'this sum, re-expressed'.

> **Test.** Cover the whole screen except the figure and whatever names it. Can the reader say what it counts, how much it is, and in whose money?

A row header naming the quantity and a column header naming the frame BOTH COUNT: that is T8's adjacent-columns pattern, it is the shape dd-006 requires, and it passes. The first draft of this test said 'the line it sits on', which would have condemned every real/nominal table we deliberately built - the wording was the agent's, not Rahul's, and it was wrong.

What fails is a figure whose noun sits in a separate block above it while its frame floats as a caption beside it - and above all, the same frame phrase doing that job for more than one quantity on the same page. That is F-12: two bold figures 500px apart, both labelled 'in today's prices', counting different things.

### dd-020 — Ask a cheap question to remove what cannot apply - never what is merely unlikely

*calculators · entry forms · answer layers · rungs · progressive disclosure*

**Do**

- `dd-020/do-1` Filter an option list by what the reader is ELIGIBLE for, and let everything lawful remain reachable.
- `dd-020/do-2` Ask a small number of cheap questions early - category, age, status - and spend the answers on removing irrelevance later.
- `dd-020/do-3` Keep an option that is uncommon but lawful, such as futures and options income for a salaried filer.
- `dd-020/do-4` Remove an option the reader cannot lawfully choose, such as 44AD or 44ADA for a salaried filer, along with the deductions that depend on it.

**Don't**

- `dd-020/dont-1` Don't hide an option because it is unlikely - unlikely is not inapplicable, and the reader it fits never learns it was there.
- `dd-020/dont-2` Don't ask a question that does not go on to remove something - a question that buys no simplification is pure cost.
- `dd-020/dont-3` Don't let a category filter change a computed answer; it removes what cannot apply, never what is inconvenient to support.

> **Test.** Take any option the category has removed and ask: is this removed because the statute forbids it, or because we guessed the reader probably will not need it? Only the first survives. If a salaried reader with F&O income, or a professional with capital gains, would be unable to enter something true about their year, the filter is wrong.
